1	// CRDT state sits beside the change log as an independent, automatically
2	// mergeable state layer. A document's CRDT type is declared with its first
3	// operation batch — "counter", "gset" (a grow-only set) or "register" (a
4	// last-writer-wins register) — and never changes afterward; two batches
5	// declaring different types concurrently serialize in one transaction and
6	// exactly one takes effect.
7	//
8	// A counter operation carries the originating device's accumulated
9	// contribution. Each device's contribution only moves forward (a regressing
10	// value is an ErrCRDTConflict and changes nothing), and the merged state is the
11	// sum of every device's maximum contribution — a PN-free grow-only counter
12	// (GCounter), so the merge is commutative, associative and idempotent.
13	//
14	// A gset operation adds elements; the merged state is the union of every
15	// accepted element, presented in ascending order. Re-adding an element does
16	// not change the state.
17	//
18	// A register operation carries an arbitrary JSON value (null, number, string,
19	// array or object, stored verbatim) and a non-negative integer version. A
20	// device's versions only move strictly forward (a regressing or equal version
21	// is an ErrCRDTConflict and changes nothing), and the merged state is the
22	// value of the operation with the greatest version, ties broken by the
23	// lexicographically smaller operation id — a last-writer-wins register whose
24	// merge is commutative, associative and idempotent, so every reader converges
25	// to the same value regardless of arrival order.
26	//
27	// An orset (observed-remove set) operation either adds one element or removes
28	// one. Every add introduces a fresh tag (its own operation id) for the
29	// element; a remove tombstones exactly the tags it observes — the adds
30	// accepted before it — and leaves later adds untouched, so a remove concurrent
31	// with an add never deletes it. Removing an element that was never added (or
32	// is already fully removed) is an accepted no-op. The merged state is the set
33	// of elements with at least one live tag, presented in ascending order; the
34	// merge is commutative, associative and idempotent, so every reader converges
35	// to the same set regardless of arrival order.
36	//
37	// Every operation carries a stable, client-supplied id, unique per document.
38	// Re-posting the same id with the same content and origin is idempotent; the
39	// same id with different content or a different device is an
40	// ErrCRDTConflict and leaves the state untouched. Operations and the merged
41	// result commit together in one serialized transaction and are durable: the
42	// decisions and the merged state are unchanged after a restart.
43	//
44	// The CRDT layer shares the registration/permission layer with the rest of the
45	// service: an unregistered device yields ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and a revoked
46	// device yields ErrPermissionDenied (403), before any CRDT content is observed.
47	// It never touches the change log, document cursors, snapshots or the
48	// subscription machinery.
49	
50	package store
51	
52	import (
53		"database/sql"
54		"encoding/json"
55		"errors"
56		"fmt"
57	)
58	
59	// CRDT document types.
60	const (
61		// CRDTTypeCounter is the grow-only counter: the merged value is the sum of
62		// each device's maximum accumulated contribution.
63		CRDTTypeCounter = "counter"
64		// CRDTTypeGSet is the grow-only set: the merged value is the union of all
65		// added elements.
66		CRDTTypeGSet = "gset"
67		// CRDTTypeRegister is the last-writer-wins register: the merged value is
68		// the value of the operation with the greatest version, ties broken by the
69		// lexicographically smaller operation id.
70		CRDTTypeRegister = "register"
71		// CRDTTypeORSet is the observed-remove set: the merged value is the set of
72		// elements with at least one add not tombstoned by an observed remove.
73		CRDTTypeORSet = "orset"
74	)
75	
76	// OR-Set operation actions.
77	const (
78		// CRDTORSetAdd adds the operation's element with a fresh tag.
79		CRDTORSetAdd = "add"
80		// CRDTORSetRemove tombstones every add tag for the element that the
81		// operation observes.
82		CRDTORSetRemove = "remove"
83	)
84	
85	// ErrCRDTNotFound reports that no CRDT operation has ever been committed for
86	// the document, so it has neither a type nor a merged state yet. The caller
87	// maps it to 404.
88	var ErrCRDTNotFound = errors.New("crdt state not found")
89	
90	// ErrCRDTConflict reports a rejected CRDT batch: the document's type is
91	// already fixed to another type, a counter contribution regressed, or an
92	// operation id already exists with different content or origin. Nothing is
93	// written; the caller maps it to 409.
94	type ErrCRDTConflict struct {
95		// ID is the conflicting operation id when one is known; it is empty for a
96		// document-level conflict (a mismatched declared type).
97		ID string
98		// Reason carries a short, machine-facing description of the conflict.
99		Reason string
100	}
101	
102	func (e *ErrCRDTConflict) Error() string {
103		if e.ID != "" {
104			return fmt.Sprintf("crdt conflict for operation %q: %s", e.ID, e.Reason)
105		}
106		return "crdt conflict: " + e.Reason
107	}
108	
109	// CRDTOp is one element of an inbound CRDT batch.
110	//
111	// For a counter, Value is the device's accumulated contribution: it must be a
112	// JSON number that is a non-negative integer, and it may never decrease for
113	// the same device. Elements and Version are unused.
114	//
115	// For a gset, Elements lists the strings the operation adds to the set and
116	// must be non-empty; Value and Version are unused.
117	//
118	// For a register, Value is an arbitrary JSON value stored verbatim and
119	// Version is a non-negative integer that must be strictly greater than every
120	// version the same device has already had accepted. Elements is unused.
121	//
122	// For an orset, Action is "add" or "remove" and Element is the non-empty
123	// string the operation adds or removes. Value, Elements and Version are
124	// unused.
125	type CRDTOp struct {
126		ID       string          // client-supplied stable id, unique per document
127		DeviceID string          // originating device (shared by the whole batch)
128		Value    json.RawMessage // counter: accumulated contribution; register: the value
129		Elements []string        // gset: elements to add
130		Version  int64           // register: logical version, per-device strictly increasing
131		Action   string          // orset: CRDTORSetAdd or CRDTORSetRemove
132		Element  string          // orset: the element the action applies to
133	}
134	
135	// CRDTState is a document's merged CRDT state.
136	//
137	// Value holds the type-specific merged result: for a counter it decodes to the
138	// JSON integer sum of per-device maxima; for a gset it decodes to the sorted
139	// JSON array of every accepted element (an empty set is []); for a register it
140	// is the winning operation's JSON value, exactly as submitted; for an orset it
141	// decodes to the sorted JSON array of the elements with at least one live add
142	// (an empty set is []).
143	type CRDTState struct {
144		Type  string          `json:"type"`
145		Value json.RawMessage `json:"value"`
146	}
147	
148	// CRDTResult reports the outcome for one element of an accepted CRDT batch.
149	type CRDTResult struct {
150		ID      string `json:"id"`
151		Created bool   `json:"created"`
152	}
153	
154	// crdtSchema is appended to the schema created in init.
155	const crdtSchema = `
156	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_documents (
157		document_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
158		type        TEXT NOT NULL
159	);
160	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_ops (
161		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
162		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
163		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
164		value       BLOB,
165		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
166	);
167	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_counter_values (
168		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
169		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
170		value       INTEGER NOT NULL,
171		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
172	);
173	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_set_elements (
174		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
175		element     TEXT NOT NULL,
176		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, element)
177	);
178	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_register_ops (
179		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
180		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
181		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
182		version     INTEGER NOT NULL,
183		value       BLOB NOT NULL,
184		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
185	);
186	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_orset_tags (
187		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
188		element     TEXT NOT NULL,
189		op_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
190		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, element, op_id)
191	);
192	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_orset_tombstones (
193		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
194		element     TEXT NOT NULL,
195		op_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
196		removed_by  TEXT NOT NULL,
197		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, element, op_id)
198	);
199	-- crdt_op_identities keeps, for each operation id whose merge row compaction
200	-- trimmed away, the only information idempotency and conflict decisions still
201	-- need: the originating device and a digest of the type-specific comparison
202	-- content. Compaction never trims this table; it does not participate in any
203	-- merge and holds a fixed-size digest rather than the operation payload, so
204	-- retaining one small row per trimmed id cannot grow the state back toward its
205	-- pre-compaction size.
206	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_op_identities (
207		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
208		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
209		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
210		digest      BLOB NOT NULL,
211		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
212	);
213	`
214	
215	// SubmitCRDTOps validates and commits one CRDT batch atomically.
216	//
217	// declaredType is the type the client asserts for the document
218	// ("counter", "gset", "register" or "orset"). It fixes the type on the document's
219	// first batch; every later batch must declare the same type. Two batches
220	// declaring different types race in one serialized transaction, so exactly
221	// one wins and the other gets an *ErrCRDTConflict (409).
222	//
223	// The device is gated first (ErrDeviceNotFound / ErrPermissionDenied) before
224	// any CRDT content is read. Every operation is then resolved against the
225	// committed history: a repeated id is idempotent only with the same device and
226	// content, otherwise it is an *ErrCRDTConflict; a counter contribution below
227	// the device's current maximum, or a register version not strictly greater
228	// than the device's accepted versions, is likewise an *ErrCRDTConflict. Any
229	// failure rejects the whole batch. Results come back in request order.
230	//
231	// When the committed batch actually moved the merged state (a counter maximum
232	// advanced, the set union grew, the register's winning value changed or the
233	// orset's live element set changed) the document's CRDT state subscribers are
234	// notified with the new merged state after the commit; idempotent repeats,
235	// rejected batches and no-op additions or removals change nothing and notify
236	// nobody.
237	func (s *Store) SubmitCRDTOps(documentID, declaredType string, ops []CRDTOp) ([]CRDTResult, error) {
238		// Serialize submissions with each other and with a subscriber's atomic
239		// register+initial-read: notifications then leave in commit order, and a
240		// committed state lands either in the initial read or in the queue.
241		s.crdtMu.Lock()
242		defer s.crdtMu.Unlock()
243	
244		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
245		if err != nil {
246			return nil, err
247		}
248		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
249	
250		deviceID := ops[0].DeviceID
251	
252		// Registration and permission are enforced before any CRDT content is
253		// observed, so a rejected submission cannot reveal type or state.
254		var deviceExists bool
255		if err := tx.QueryRow(
256			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
257		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
258			return nil, err
259		}
260		if !deviceExists {
261			return nil, ErrDeviceNotFound
262		}
263		var storedAuth int
264		err = tx.QueryRow(
265			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
266			documentID, deviceID,
267		).Scan(&storedAuth)
268		switch {
269		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
270			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
271		case err != nil:
272			return nil, err
273		default:
274			if storedAuth == 0 {
275				return nil, ErrPermissionDenied
276			}
277		}
278	
279		// Resolve the document type: fixed on the first accepted batch.
280		var docType string
281		err = tx.QueryRow(
282			`SELECT type FROM crdt_documents WHERE document_id = ?`, documentID,
283		).Scan(&docType)
284		switch {
285		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
286			// First batch for this document: its declared type wins the race.
287			if _, err := tx.Exec(
288				`INSERT INTO crdt_documents (document_id, type) VALUES (?, ?)`,
289				documentID, declaredType,
290			); err != nil {
291				return nil, err
292			}
293			docType = declaredType
294		case err != nil:
295			return nil, err
296		default:
297			if docType != declaredType {
298				return nil, &ErrCRDTConflict{
299					Reason: fmt.Sprintf("document type is already %q", docType),
300				}
301			}
302		}
303	
304		results := make([]CRDTResult, len(ops))
305	
306		var stateChanged bool
307		switch docType {
308		case CRDTTypeCounter:
309			changed, err := applyCounterOps(tx, documentID, ops, results)
310			if err != nil {
311				return nil, err
312			}
313			stateChanged = changed
314		case CRDTTypeGSet:
315			changed, err := applyGSetOps(tx, documentID, ops, results)
316			if err != nil {
317				return nil, err
318			}
319			stateChanged = changed
320		case CRDTTypeRegister:
321			changed, err := applyRegisterOps(tx, documentID, ops, results)
322			if err != nil {
323				return nil, err
324			}
325			stateChanged = changed
326		case CRDTTypeORSet:
327			changed, err := applyORSetOps(tx, documentID, ops, results)
328			if err != nil {
329				return nil, err
330			}
331			stateChanged = changed
332		}
333	
334		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
335			return nil, err
336		}
337		if stateChanged {
338			// The committed batch moved the merged state; re-derive it (the merge
339			// is never cached) and publish it after commit, so a subscriber only
340			// ever observes a durable state and commits arrive in commit order.
341			state, err := s.GetCRDTState(documentID)
342			if err != nil {
343				return results, nil
344			}
345			s.notifyCRDTSubscribers(documentID, state)
346		}
347		return results, nil
348	}
349	
350	// applyCounterOps resolves and applies every counter operation inside tx. A
351	// repeated id is idempotent only with the same device and contribution. A new
352	// id with a contribution below the device's stored maximum regresses the
353	// counter and is rejected; an equal contribution is an accepted no-op; a
354	// larger one advances the device's maximum. It reports whether the merged
355	// state actually changed — only an advancing contribution moves the sum.
356	func applyCounterOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, ops []CRDTOp, results []CRDTResult) (bool, error) {
357		changed := false
358		for i, op := range ops {
359			value, err := decodeCounterValue(op.Value)
360			if err != nil {
361				return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{ID: op.ID, Reason: err.Error()}
362			}
363	
364			var existingDevice string
365			var existingValue []byte
366			err = tx.QueryRow(
367				`SELECT device_id, value FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
368				documentID, op.ID,
369			).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingValue)
370			switch {
371			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
372				// The merge row may have been trimmed by compaction; the retained
373				// identity still decides between idempotent replay and conflict.
374				idempotent, idErr := resolveTrimmedIdentity(
375					tx, documentID, CRDTTypeCounter,
376					"operation id already exists with a different device or value", op,
377				)
378				if idErr != nil {
379					return false, idErr
380				}
381				if idempotent {
382					results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
383					continue
384				}
385				// New id: enforce monotonicity against this device's maximum.
386				var current sql.NullInt64
387				if scanErr := tx.QueryRow(
388					`SELECT value FROM crdt_counter_values WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
389					documentID, op.DeviceID,
390				).Scan(&current); scanErr != nil && !errors.Is(scanErr, sql.ErrNoRows) {
391					return false, scanErr
392				}
393				if current.Valid && value < current.Int64 {
394					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
395						ID:     op.ID,
396						Reason: "counter contribution must not decrease",
397					}
398				}
399				if _, err := tx.Exec(
400					`INSERT INTO crdt_ops (document_id, id, device_id, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
401					documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, []byte(op.Value),
402				); err != nil {
403					return false, err
404				}
405				if !current.Valid || value > current.Int64 {
406					if _, err := tx.Exec(
407						`INSERT INTO crdt_counter_values (document_id, device_id, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
408						 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value`,
409						documentID, op.DeviceID, value,
410					); err != nil {
411						return false, err
412					}
413					changed = true
414				}
415				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: true}
416			case err != nil:
417				return false, err
418			default:
419				if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || !jsonEqual(existingValue, op.Value) {
420					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
421						ID:     op.ID,
422						Reason: "operation id already exists with a different device or value",
423					}
424				}
425				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
426			}
427		}
428		return changed, nil
429	}
430	
431	// applyGSetOps resolves and applies every grow-only-set operation inside tx.
432	// A repeated id is idempotent only with the same device and the same set of
433	// elements (element order is irrelevant to the merge). New elements are
434	// inserted into the union table; re-adding an element changes nothing. It
435	// reports whether the merged state actually changed — only an element that
436	// was not already in the union moves it.
437	func applyGSetOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, ops []CRDTOp, results []CRDTResult) (bool, error) {
438		changed := false
439		for i, op := range ops {
440			var existingDevice string
441			var existingElements []byte
442			err := tx.QueryRow(
443				`SELECT device_id, value FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
444				documentID, op.ID,
445			).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingElements)
446			switch {
447			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
448				// The operation row covering the union may have been trimmed; the
449				// retained identity still decides replay versus conflict.
450				idempotent, idErr := resolveTrimmedIdentity(
451					tx, documentID, CRDTTypeGSet,
452					"operation id already exists with a different device or elements", op,
453				)
454				if idErr != nil {
455					return false, idErr
456				}
457				if idempotent {
458					results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
459					continue
460				}
461				// New id; insert the op and its elements below.
462			case err != nil:
463				return false, err
464			default:
465				if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || !stringSetEqual(existingElements, op.Elements) {
466					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
467						ID:     op.ID,
468						Reason: "operation id already exists with a different device or elements",
469					}
470				}
471				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
472				continue
473			}
474	
475			if _, err := tx.Exec(
476				`INSERT INTO crdt_ops (document_id, id, device_id, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
477				documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, []byte(encodeSetElements(op.Elements)),
478			); err != nil {
479				return false, err
480			}
481			for _, element := range op.Elements {
482				// The union table is an identity insert: a repeated element simply
483				// exists once, and only a genuinely new element moves the merge.
484				res, err := tx.Exec(
485					`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO crdt_set_elements (document_id, element) VALUES (?, ?)`,
486					documentID, element,
487				)
488				if err != nil {
489					return false, err
490				}
491				if n, err := res.RowsAffected(); err == nil && n > 0 {
492					changed = true
493				}
494			}
495			results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: true}
496		}
497		return changed, nil
498	}
499	
500	// applyRegisterOps resolves and applies every register operation inside tx. A
501	// repeated id is idempotent only with the same device, version and value. A
502	// new id whose version is not strictly greater than every version already
503	// accepted from the same device regresses (or stalls) the device's clock and
504	// is rejected. It reports whether the merged state actually changed — only a
505	// change of the winning operation's value moves it.
506	func applyRegisterOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, ops []CRDTOp, results []CRDTResult) (bool, error) {
507		// The merged value before the batch, so a batch that leaves the winner's
508		// value untouched (an idempotent replay, or a new op that loses the
509		// last-writer-wins comparison) reports no change and notifies nobody.
510		prev, prevOK, err := registerWinner(tx, documentID)
511		if err != nil {
512			return false, err
513		}
514	
515		for i, op := range ops {
516			if op.Version < 0 {
517				// The API boundary rejects negative versions; a negative version
518				// here means the caller skipped validation.
519				return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{ID: op.ID, Reason: "register version must be a non-negative integer"}
520			}
521	
522			var existingDevice string
523			var existingVersion int64
524			var existingValue []byte
525			err := tx.QueryRow(
526				`SELECT device_id, version, value FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
527				documentID, op.ID,
528			).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingVersion, &existingValue)
529			switch {
530			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
531				// An older per-device version may have been trimmed; the retained
532				// identity still decides replay versus conflict before the version
533				// monotonicity gate, which only applies to an id never accepted.
534				idempotent, idErr := resolveTrimmedIdentity(
535					tx, documentID, CRDTTypeRegister,
536					"operation id already exists with a different device, version or value", op,
537				)
538				if idErr != nil {
539					return false, idErr
540				}
541				if idempotent {
542					results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
543					continue
544				}
545				// New id: the device's versions only move strictly forward. The
546				// per-device maximum is derived from the retained operations, so
547				// the decision survives compaction (which keeps each device's
548				// latest) and restarts without extra state.
549				var maxVersion sql.NullInt64
550				if scanErr := tx.QueryRow(
551					`SELECT MAX(version) FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
552					documentID, op.DeviceID,
553				).Scan(&maxVersion); scanErr != nil {
554					return false, scanErr
555				}
556				if maxVersion.Valid && op.Version <= maxVersion.Int64 {
557					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
558						ID:     op.ID,
559						Reason: "register version must be greater than the device's previously accepted version",
560					}
561				}
562				if _, err := tx.Exec(
563					`INSERT INTO crdt_register_ops (document_id, id, device_id, version, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
564					documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, op.Version, []byte(op.Value),
565				); err != nil {
566					return false, err
567				}
568				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: true}
569			case err != nil:
570				return false, err
571			default:
572				if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || existingVersion != op.Version || !jsonEqual(existingValue, op.Value) {
573					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
574						ID:     op.ID,
575						Reason: "operation id already exists with a different device, version or value",
576					}
577				}
578				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
579			}
580		}
581	
582		next, nextOK, err := registerWinner(tx, documentID)
583		if err != nil {
584			return false, err
585		}
586		// The merge is the winner's value; a new winner carrying a JSON-equal
587		// value does not move the state.
588		changed := prevOK != nextOK || (prevOK && nextOK && !jsonEqual(prev, next))
589		return changed, nil
590	}
591	
592	// registerWinner returns the value the register currently merges to: the
593	// value of the accepted operation with the greatest version, ties broken by
594	// the lexicographically smaller operation id. It reports false when the
595	// document has no accepted register operation yet.
596	func registerWinner(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) (json.RawMessage, bool, error) {
597		var value []byte
598		err := tx.QueryRow(
599			`SELECT value FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ?
600			 ORDER BY version DESC, id ASC LIMIT 1`,
601			documentID,
602		).Scan(&value)
603		switch {
604		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
605			return nil, false, nil
606		case err != nil:
607			return nil, false, err
608		default:
609			return json.RawMessage(value), true, nil
610		}
611	}
612	
613	// applyORSetOps resolves and applies every observed-remove-set operation
614	// inside tx. A repeated id is idempotent only with the same device, action and
615	// element; an idempotent replay applies nothing, so a replayed remove never
616	// tombstones adds that landed after its first acceptance. An add tags the
617	// element with its own operation id; a remove tombstones exactly the tags
618	// already accepted for the element — adds that arrive later carry fresh tags
619	// and are unaffected, and removing an element with no live (or no) tags is an
620	// accepted no-op. It reports whether the merged state actually changed — only
621	// a change in the set of elements with at least one live tag moves it.
622	func applyORSetOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, ops []CRDTOp, results []CRDTResult) (bool, error) {
623		// The merged element set before the batch, so a batch that leaves it
624		// untouched (an idempotent replay, an add of an already-present element,
625		// a remove with nothing observed) reports no change and notifies nobody.
626		prev, err := queryORSetElements(tx, documentID)
627		if err != nil {
628			return false, err
629		}
630	
631		for i, op := range ops {
632			if op.Action != CRDTORSetAdd && op.Action != CRDTORSetRemove {
633				// The API boundary rejects unknown actions; one here means the
634				// caller skipped validation.
635				return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{ID: op.ID, Reason: `orset action must be "add" or "remove"`}
636			}
637	
638			var existingDevice string
639			var existingContent []byte
640			err := tx.QueryRow(
641				`SELECT device_id, value FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
642				documentID, op.ID,
643			).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingContent)
644			switch {
645			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
646				// New id; insert the op and apply its effect below.
647			case err != nil:
648				return false, err
649			default:
650				if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || !jsonEqual(existingContent, encodeORSetContent(op.Action, op.Element)) {
651					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
652						ID:     op.ID,
653						Reason: "operation id already exists with a different device, action or element",
654					}
655				}
656				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
657				continue
658			}
659	
660			if _, err := tx.Exec(
661				`INSERT INTO crdt_ops (document_id, id, device_id, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
662				documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, []byte(encodeORSetContent(op.Action, op.Element)),
663			); err != nil {
664				return false, err
665			}
666			if op.Action == CRDTORSetAdd {
667				// The tag is the operation id itself: unique per document, so the
668				// insert always lands and concurrent adds of the same element
669				// accumulate independent tags.
670				if _, err := tx.Exec(
671					`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO crdt_orset_tags (document_id, element, op_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
672					documentID, op.Element, op.ID,
673				); err != nil {
674					return false, err
675				}
676			} else {
677				// Tombstone exactly the tags this remove observes: the adds
678				// accepted before it. Tags created later are not in the table yet
679				// and survive; already-tombstoned tags are an identity insert.
680				if _, err := tx.Exec(
681					`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO crdt_orset_tombstones (document_id, element, op_id, removed_by)
682					 SELECT ?, ?, op_id, ? FROM crdt_orset_tags
683					 WHERE document_id = ? AND element = ?`,
684					documentID, op.Element, op.ID, documentID, op.Element,
685				); err != nil {
686					return false, err
687				}
688			}
689			results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: true}
690		}
691	
692		next, err := queryORSetElements(tx, documentID)
693		if err != nil {
694			return false, err
695		}
696		return !stringSliceEqual(prev, next), nil
697	}
698	
699	// orsetLiveElementsSQL selects the elements with at least one add tag no
700	// tombstone covers, in ascending order — the orset merge, derived from the
701	// accepted operations rather than cached.
702	const orsetLiveElementsSQL = `
703	SELECT DISTINCT element FROM crdt_orset_tags t
704	WHERE t.document_id = ? AND NOT EXISTS (
705		SELECT 1 FROM crdt_orset_tombstones x
706		WHERE x.document_id = t.document_id
707		  AND x.element = t.element
708		  AND x.op_id = t.op_id
709	)
710	ORDER BY element ASC`
711	
712	// orsetQuerier is satisfied by both *sql.Tx (inside a submission) and *sql.DB
713	// (a state read), so the merge query exists exactly once.
714	type orsetQuerier interface {
715		Query(query string, args ...any) (*sql.Rows, error)
716	}
717	
718	// queryORSetElements returns the document's live orset elements in ascending
719	// order. The empty set is an empty slice, never nil, so it marshals as [].
720	func queryORSetElements(q orsetQuerier, documentID string) ([]string, error) {
721		rows, err := q.Query(orsetLiveElementsSQL, documentID)
722		if err != nil {
723			return nil, err
724		}
725		elements := make([]string, 0)
726		for rows.Next() {
727			var element string
728			if err := rows.Scan(&element); err != nil {
729				_ = rows.Close()
730				return nil, err
731			}
732			elements = append(elements, element)
733		}
734		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
735			_ = rows.Close()
736			return nil, err
737		}
738		_ = rows.Close()
739		return elements, nil
740	}
741	
742	// encodeORSetContent renders an orset operation's content (its action and
743	// element) as a JSON object for durable storage, so a later submission of the
744	// same id can be compared against the original content.
745	func encodeORSetContent(action, element string) json.RawMessage {
746		raw, err := json.Marshal(struct {
747			Action  string `json:"action"`
748			Element string `json:"element"`
749		}{Action: action, Element: element})
750		if err != nil {
751			// Strings always marshal.
752			return json.RawMessage(`{"action":"","element":""}`)
753		}
754		return raw
755	}
756	
757	// stringSliceEqual reports whether a and b hold the same strings in the same
758	// order. Both orset element lists are ascending, so order-sensitive equality
759	// is set equality.
760	func stringSliceEqual(a, b []string) bool {
761		if len(a) != len(b) {
762			return false
763		}
764		for i := range a {
765			if a[i] != b[i] {
766				return false
767			}
768		}
769		return true
770	}
771	
772	// decodeCounterValue requires raw to be a non-negative JSON integer with no
773	// fraction or exponent. Floats, strings, booleans and null are rejected at the
774	// API boundary; a malformed integer here means the caller skipped validation.
775	func decodeCounterValue(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, error) {
776		var n int64
777		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
778			return 0, errors.New("counter value must be a non-negative integer")
779		}
780		return n, nil
781	}
782	
783	// encodeSetElements renders the elements of one gset operation as a JSON array
784	// for durable storage of the original operation content.
785	func encodeSetElements(elements []string) json.RawMessage {
786		raw, err := json.Marshal(elements)
787		if err != nil {
788			// Strings always marshal.
789			return json.RawMessage("[]")
790		}
791		return raw
792	}
793	
794	// stringSetEqual reports whether raw (a JSON array of strings stored for a
795	// prior gset operation) contains exactly the elements of want, ignoring
796	// duplicates and order: the content of a set operation is the set of elements.
797	func stringSetEqual(raw json.RawMessage, want []string) bool {
798		var got []string
799		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &got); err != nil {
800			return false
801		}
802		set := make(map[string]struct{}, len(got))
803		for _, e := range got {
804			set[e] = struct{}{}
805		}
806		for _, e := range want {
807			if _, ok := set[e]; !ok {
808				return false
809			}
810			delete(set, e)
811		}
812		return len(set) == 0
813	}
814	
815	// GetCRDTState returns the merged CRDT state for documentID. A document with
816	// no committed operations yields ErrCRDTNotFound (the caller answers 404).
817	//
818	// The merged value is derived from the per-device maxima (counter), the union
819	// table (gset), the version/id ordering of the accepted operations (register)
820	// or the live tags minus tombstones (orset), not cached: it is exactly what
821	// any equivalent batch order would converge to.
822	func (s *Store) GetCRDTState(documentID string) (CRDTState, error) {
823		var docType string
824		err := s.db.QueryRow(
825			`SELECT type FROM crdt_documents WHERE document_id = ?`, documentID,
826		).Scan(&docType)
827		switch {
828		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
829			return CRDTState{}, ErrCRDTNotFound
830		case err != nil:
831			return CRDTState{}, err
832		}
833	
834		switch docType {
835		case CRDTTypeCounter:
836			var total int64
837			if err := s.db.QueryRow(
838				`SELECT COALESCE(SUM(value), 0) FROM crdt_counter_values WHERE document_id = ?`,
839				documentID,
840			).Scan(&total); err != nil {
841				return CRDTState{}, err
842			}
843			raw, err := json.Marshal(total)
844			if err != nil {
845				return CRDTState{}, err
846			}
847			return CRDTState{Type: docType, Value: raw}, nil
848		case CRDTTypeGSet:
849			rows, err := s.db.Query(
850				`SELECT element FROM crdt_set_elements WHERE document_id = ? ORDER BY element ASC`,
851				documentID,
852			)

855			}

873			}

875		case CRDTTypeRegister:
876			// A document's type row commits together with its first batch, so a
877			// register document always has at least one accepted operation.
878			var value []byte
879			if err := s.db.QueryRow(
880				`SELECT value FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ?
881				 ORDER BY version DESC, id ASC LIMIT 1`,
882				documentID,
883			).Scan(&value); err != nil {
884				return CRDTState{}, err
885			}
886			return CRDTState{Type: docType, Value: json.RawMessage(value)}, nil
887		case CRDTTypeORSet:
888			elements, err := queryORSetElements(s.db, documentID)
889			if err != nil {
890				return CRDTState{}, err
891			}
892			raw, err := json.Marshal(elements)
893			if err != nil {
894				return CRDTState{}, err
895			}
896			return CRDTState{Type: docType, Value: raw}, nil
897		default:
898			return CRDTState{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown crdt type %q stored for document", docType)
899		}

1	// CRDT compaction and snapshot reads bound the storage a long-lived document
2	// accumulates in the CRDT state layer. Merges only ever need a small part of
3	// the accepted history: a counter merges from each device's maximum
4	// contribution, a gset from the element union, a register from each device's
5	// latest version and the winner among them, and an orset from its live tags
6	// and the tombstones covering dead ones. Everything else — superseded counter
7	// contributions, gset operations whose elements later operations also carry,
8	// older register versions, tombstoned orset tags and the tombstones covering
9	// them — no longer affects the merged result and can be trimmed.
10	//
11	// Compaction rewrites nothing outside the CRDT tables: it never allocates a
12	// change cursor, never writes a change record and never notifies subscribers,
13	// because the merged value does not move. The trimmed state still reproduces
14	// the exact merge and still answers the submission layer's questions — the
15	// per-device counter maxima and register versions that gate regressions live
16	// in the retained rows, and the device plus comparison content of every
17	// trimmed operation id moves into the small crdt_op_identities table — so
18	// merge results, idempotency decisions and conflict responses are computed by
19	// the same rules afterward. A snapshot read reports the merged value together
20	// with the number of stored operations and tombstones, so a client can observe
21	// what compaction trimmed; both counts are non-negative and durable across
22	// restarts. The identity table is neither count: it holds one fixed-size
23	// digest per trimmed id, never participates in a merge, and cannot grow the
24	// trimmed state back toward its pre-compaction size.
25	
26	package store
27	
28	import (
29		"database/sql"
30		"encoding/json"
31		"errors"
32	)
33	
34	// CRDTSnapshot is a document's merged CRDT state together with the storage
35	// footprint of that state: Operations counts the stored operations the merge
36	// is derived from (counter and gset: rows of the operation log; register: the
37	// retained per-device operations; orset: the add tags, live or tombstoned)
38	// and Tombstones counts the stored orset tombstones (always zero for the
39	// other types). Both counts are non-negative; compaction drives them down to
40	// the operations and tombstones that still participate in the merge.
41	type CRDTSnapshot struct {
42		Type       string          // the document's fixed CRDT type
43		Value      json.RawMessage // the merged value, exactly as GetCRDTState derives it
44		Operations int64           // stored operations the merge is derived from
45		Tombstones int64           // stored orset tombstones; 0 for counter, gset and register
46	}
47	
48	// CompactCRDT trims every stored operation and tombstone that no longer
49	// affects the document's merged result, in one serialized transaction, and
50	// returns the post-compaction snapshot (byte-for-byte what a snapshot read
51	// returns immediately afterward).
52	//
53	// The registration/permission layer is enforced exactly as in SubmitCRDTOps
54	// and before any CRDT content is observed: an unregistered device yields
55	// ErrDeviceNotFound and a revoked device yields ErrPermissionDenied, and
56	// neither touches any state. A document with no committed CRDT operation
57	// yields ErrCRDTNotFound. Any failure leaves the state untouched.
58	//
59	// Per type, compaction keeps precisely the rows the merge and the submission
60	// checks still read:
61	//
62	//   - counter: each device's maximum contribution (ties keep the
63	//     lexicographically smaller operation id); superseded contributions are
64	//     dropped. The per-device maxima table is untouched, so monotonicity
65	//     checks and the merged sum are unchanged. Each dropped id keeps a
66	//     device-plus-value identity.
67	//   - gset: a minimal prefix cover of the union — operations are considered
68	//     in ascending id order and one is kept only when it contributes an
69	//     element no previously kept operation covers. The union table is
70	//     untouched, so the merged set is unchanged. Each dropped id keeps a
71	//     device-plus-elements identity.
72	//   - register: each device's greatest-version operation (which includes the
73	//     document's winner). Regression checks derive per-device maxima from
74	//     these rows, so later version checks and the winning value are
75	//     unchanged. Each dropped older id keeps a device-plus-version-plus-value
76	//     identity.
77	//   - orset: live add tags. Tombstoned tags are dropped together with the
78	//     tombstones covering them — a dead tag and its tombstone cancel out of
79	//     the merge — so the live element set is unchanged. The operation log is
80	//     untouched (adds and removes alike), so replaying either one stays
81	//     idempotent and a replayed remove never tombstones tags that arrived
82	//     after it; no identity row is needed.
83	//
84	// Compaction is idempotent: a second run finds nothing to trim and returns
85	// the same snapshot. It commits no change-log row, allocates no cursor and,
86	// because the merged value never moves, notifies no subscriber.
87	func (s *Store) CompactCRDT(documentID, deviceID string) (CRDTSnapshot, error) {
88		// Serialize with submissions and other compactions: the trim and the
89		// submission checks read the same rows, so they must not interleave.
90		s.crdtMu.Lock()
91		defer s.crdtMu.Unlock()
92	
93		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
94		if err != nil {
95			return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
96		}
97		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
98	
99		// Registration and permission are enforced before any CRDT content is
100		// observed, so a rejected compaction cannot reveal type or state.
101		var deviceExists bool
102		if err := tx.QueryRow(
103			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
104		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
105			return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
106		}
107		if !deviceExists {
108			return CRDTSnapshot{}, ErrDeviceNotFound
109		}
110		var storedAuth int
111		err = tx.QueryRow(
112			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
113			documentID, deviceID,
114		).Scan(&storedAuth)
115		switch {
116		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
117			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
118		case err != nil:
119			return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
120		default:
121			if storedAuth == 0 {
122				return CRDTSnapshot{}, ErrPermissionDenied
123			}
124		}
125	
126		var docType string
127		err = tx.QueryRow(
128			`SELECT type FROM crdt_documents WHERE document_id = ?`, documentID,
129		).Scan(&docType)
130		switch {
131		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
132			return CRDTSnapshot{}, ErrCRDTNotFound
133		case err != nil:
134			return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
135		}
136	
137		switch docType {
138		case CRDTTypeCounter:
139			if err := compactCounterOps(tx, documentID); err != nil {
140				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
141			}
142		case CRDTTypeGSet:
143			if err := compactGSetOps(tx, documentID); err != nil {
144				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
145			}
146		case CRDTTypeRegister:
147			if err := compactRegisterOps(tx, documentID); err != nil {
148				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
149			}
150		case CRDTTypeORSet:
151			if err := compactORSetOps(tx, documentID); err != nil {
152				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
153			}
154		}
155	
156		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
157			return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
158		}
159		// The commit is durable and crdtMu is still held, so no submission or
160		// compaction can interleave before this read: the returned snapshot is
161		// exactly what a snapshot read immediately afterward observes.
162		return s.GetCRDTSnapshot(documentID)
163	}
164	
165	// compactCounterOps drops every counter operation superseded by a greater (or
166	// equal but later-id) contribution from the same device, keeping exactly one
167	// operation per device: its maximum contribution, ties broken by the
168	// lexicographically smaller operation id. The per-device maxima table that
169	// drives the merge and the regression checks is untouched. Before a row is
170	// dropped its identity is retained, so a replay of the trimmed id stays
171	// idempotent and a mismatched replay stays a conflict.
172	func compactCounterOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) error {
173		rows, err := tx.Query(
174			`SELECT id, device_id, value FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC`,
175			documentID,
176		)
177		if err != nil {
178			return err
179		}
180		type contribution struct {
181			id    string
182			value int64
183			raw   []byte
184		}
185		best := make(map[string]contribution)
186		var drop []CRDTOp
187		for rows.Next() {
188			var id, deviceID string
189			var raw []byte
190			if err := rows.Scan(&id, &deviceID, &raw); err != nil {
191				_ = rows.Close()
192				return err
193			}
194			value, err := decodeCounterValue(raw)
195			if err != nil {
196				_ = rows.Close()
197				return err
198			}
199			// Ids arrive in ascending order, so the first contribution seen at the
200			// device's maximum value carries the smallest id; only a strictly
201			// greater value replaces it.
202			if cur, ok := best[deviceID]; !ok || value > cur.value {
203				if ok {
204					drop = append(drop, CRDTOp{ID: cur.id, DeviceID: deviceID, Value: json.RawMessage(cur.raw)})
205				}
206				best[deviceID] = contribution{id: id, value: value, raw: raw}
207			} else {
208				drop = append(drop, CRDTOp{ID: id, DeviceID: deviceID, Value: json.RawMessage(raw)})
209			}
210		}
211		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
212			_ = rows.Close()
213			return err
214		}
215		_ = rows.Close()
216	
217		for _, op := range drop {
218			if err := retainCRDTOpIdentity(tx, documentID, CRDTTypeCounter, op); err != nil {
219				return err
220			}
221			if _, err := tx.Exec(
222				`DELETE FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
223				documentID, op.ID,
224			); err != nil {
225				return err
226			}
227		}
228		return nil
229	}
230	
231	// compactGSetOps drops every gset operation whose elements are all covered by
232	// kept operations: operations are considered in ascending id order and one is
233	// kept only when it contributes at least one element no previously kept
234	// operation covers. The union table that drives the merge is untouched, so
235	// the kept operations still reproduce the exact merged set. A dropped
236	// operation's identity is retained before its row is deleted, so a replay of
237	// the trimmed id stays idempotent and a mismatched replay stays a conflict.
238	func compactGSetOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) error {
239		rows, err := tx.Query(
240			`SELECT id, device_id, value FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC`,
241			documentID,
242		)
243		if err != nil {
244			return err
245		}
246		covered := make(map[string]struct{})
247		var drop []CRDTOp
248		for rows.Next() {
249			var id, deviceID string
250			var raw []byte
251			if err := rows.Scan(&id, &deviceID, &raw); err != nil {
252				_ = rows.Close()
253				return err
254			}
255			var elements []string
256			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &elements); err != nil {
257				_ = rows.Close()
258				return err
259			}
260			keeps := false
261			for _, element := range elements {
262				if _, ok := covered[element]; !ok {
263					keeps = true
264					covered[element] = struct{}{}
265				}
266			}
267			if !keeps {
268				drop = append(drop, CRDTOp{ID: id, DeviceID: deviceID, Elements: elements})
269			}
270		}
271		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
272			_ = rows.Close()
273			return err
274		}
275		_ = rows.Close()
276	
277		for _, op := range drop {
278			if err := retainCRDTOpIdentity(tx, documentID, CRDTTypeGSet, op); err != nil {
279				return err
280			}
281			if _, err := tx.Exec(
282				`DELETE FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
283				documentID, op.ID,
284			); err != nil {
285				return err
286			}
287		}
288		return nil
289	}
290	
291	// compactRegisterOps drops every register operation superseded by a greater
292	// version from the same device, keeping each device's greatest-version
293	// operation. Versions strictly increase per device, so exactly one row per
294	// device survives; the per-device maxima the regression checks derive from
295	// the table, and the document's winning value, are unchanged. A dropped
296	// operation's identity is retained before its row is deleted, so a replay of
297	// the trimmed id stays idempotent and a mismatched replay stays a conflict.
298	func compactRegisterOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) error {
299		rows, err := tx.Query(
300			`SELECT id, device_id, version, value FROM crdt_register_ops
301			 WHERE document_id = ?
302			   AND EXISTS (
303				SELECT 1 FROM crdt_register_ops newer
304				WHERE newer.document_id = crdt_register_ops.document_id
305				  AND newer.device_id = crdt_register_ops.device_id
306				  AND newer.version > crdt_register_ops.version
307			   )`,
308			documentID,
309		)
310		if err != nil {
311			return err
312		}
313		var drop []CRDTOp
314		for rows.Next() {
315			var op CRDTOp
316			if err := rows.Scan(&op.ID, &op.DeviceID, &op.Version, &op.Value); err != nil {
317				_ = rows.Close()
318				return err
319			}
320			drop = append(drop, op)
321		}
322		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
323			_ = rows.Close()
324			return err
325		}
326		_ = rows.Close()
327	
328		for _, op := range drop {
329			if err := retainCRDTOpIdentity(tx, documentID, CRDTTypeRegister, op); err != nil {
330				return err
331			}
332			if _, err := tx.Exec(
333				`DELETE FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
334				documentID, op.ID,
335			); err != nil {
336				return err
337			}
338		}
339		return nil
340	}
341	
342	// compactORSetOps drops every tombstoned add tag together with every
343	// tombstone: a dead tag and the tombstone covering it cancel out of the
344	// merge, so the live element set is unchanged. The operation log is
345	// untouched, so replaying an add or a remove stays idempotent and a replayed
346	// remove never tombstones tags accepted after it.
347	func compactORSetOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) error {
348		if _, err := tx.Exec(
349			`DELETE FROM crdt_orset_tags
350			 WHERE document_id = ?
351			   AND EXISTS (
352				SELECT 1 FROM crdt_orset_tombstones x
353				WHERE x.document_id = crdt_orset_tags.document_id
354				  AND x.element = crdt_orset_tags.element
355				  AND x.op_id = crdt_orset_tags.op_id
356			   )`,
357			documentID,
358		); err != nil {
359			return err
360		}
361		_, err := tx.Exec(
362			`DELETE FROM crdt_orset_tombstones WHERE document_id = ?`,
363			documentID,
364		)
365		return err
366	}
367	
368	// GetCRDTSnapshot returns the document's merged CRDT state together with the
369	// number of stored operations and tombstones the merge is derived from. A
370	// document with no committed operations yields ErrCRDTNotFound (the caller
371	// answers 404). The read is pure: it advances no cursor, writes nothing and
372	// registers no subscription.
373	func (s *Store) GetCRDTSnapshot(documentID string) (CRDTSnapshot, error) {
374		state, err := s.GetCRDTState(documentID)
375		if err != nil {
376			return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
377		}
378		snapshot := CRDTSnapshot{Type: state.Type, Value: state.Value}
379	
380		count := func(query string) (int64, error) {
381			var n int64
382			if err := s.db.QueryRow(query, documentID).Scan(&n); err != nil {
383				return 0, err
384			}
385			return n, nil
386		}
387	
388		switch state.Type {
389		case CRDTTypeCounter, CRDTTypeGSet:
390			operations, err := count(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ?`)
391			if err != nil {
392				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
393			}
394			snapshot.Operations = operations
395		case CRDTTypeRegister:
396			operations, err := count(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ?`)
397			if err != nil {
398				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
399			}
400			snapshot.Operations = operations
401		case CRDTTypeORSet:
402			operations, err := count(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM crdt_orset_tags WHERE document_id = ?`)
403			if err != nil {
404				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
405			}
406			tombstones, err := count(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM crdt_orset_tombstones WHERE document_id = ?`)
407			if err != nil {
408				return CRDTSnapshot{}, err
409			}
410			snapshot.Operations = operations
411			snapshot.Tombstones = tombstones
412		}
413		return snapshot, nil
414	}

1	// Accepted-operation identities keep idempotency and conflict decisions
2	// working after compaction. Compaction trims the rows a merge derives its
3	// result from — superseded counter contributions, covered gset operations,
4	// older register versions, dead orset tags and their tombstones — but a
5	// re-submitted operation id must still be recognized. When a row is trimmed,
6	// compaction moves the only information that decision compares — the
7	// originating device and a digest of the type-specific comparison content —
8	// into crdt_op_identities. Untrimmed ids keep answering from their merge row,
9	// so the table holds one small fixed-size record per trimmed id, never one per
10	// accepted operation: it cannot grow the trimmed state back toward its
11	// pre-compaction footprint.
12	//
13	// The table never participates in a merge: the counter sum, the set union,
14	// the register winner and the live orset tags are all derived without it.
15	
16	package store
17	
18	import (
19		"bytes"
20		"crypto/sha256"
21		"database/sql"
22		"encoding/json"
23		"errors"
24		"sort"
25	)
26	
27	// canonicalOpDigest renders the type-specific comparison content of op in a
28	// single canonical form and hashes it, prefixed by the type so contents of
29	// different types never collide. Two submissions of one id carry the same
30	// digest exactly when the submission layer's existing equality rules accept
31	// the second as idempotent:
32	//
33	//   - counter: the decoded non-negative integer (client formatting ignored);
34	//   - gset: the element set (order and duplicates ignored), rendered as a
35	//     sorted unique JSON array;
36	//   - register: the version together with the JSON-semantic value (1 and 1.0
37	//     and reordered object keys compare equal, as in jsonEqual);
38	//   - orset: the action and the element.
39	func canonicalOpDigest(docType string, op CRDTOp) ([]byte, error) {
40		var content []byte
41		switch docType {
42		case CRDTTypeCounter:
43			n, err := decodeCounterValue(op.Value)
44			if err != nil {
45				return nil, err
46			}
47			raw, err := json.Marshal(n)
48			if err != nil {
49				return nil, err
50			}
51			content = raw
52		case CRDTTypeGSet:
53			set := make(map[string]struct{}, len(op.Elements))
54			for _, element := range op.Elements {
55				set[element] = struct{}{}
56			}
57			elements := make([]string, 0, len(set))
58			for element := range set {
59				elements = append(elements, element)
60			}
61			sort.Strings(elements)
62			raw, err := json.Marshal(elements)
63			if err != nil {
64				return nil, err
65			}
66			content = raw
67		case CRDTTypeRegister:
68			if op.Version < 0 {
69				return nil, errors.New("register version must be a non-negative integer")
70			}
71			var value any
72			if err := json.Unmarshal(op.Value, &value); err != nil {
73				return nil, err
74			}
75			// Re-marshaling the decoded value canonicalizes whitespace and object
76			// key order exactly the way jsonEqual compares values; wrapping it in a
77			// fixed-field struct folds the version into the same canonical bytes.
78			valueBytes, err := json.Marshal(value)
79			if err != nil {
80				return nil, err
81			}
82			raw, err := json.Marshal(struct {
83				Version int64           `json:"version"`
84				Value   json.RawMessage `json:"value"`
85			}{Version: op.Version, Value: json.RawMessage(valueBytes)})
86			if err != nil {
87				return nil, err
88			}
89			content = raw
90		case CRDTTypeORSet:
91			if op.Action != CRDTORSetAdd && op.Action != CRDTORSetRemove {
92				return nil, errors.New(`orset action must be "add" or "remove"`)
93			}
94			content = []byte(encodeORSetContent(op.Action, op.Element))
95		default:
96			return nil, errors.New("unknown crdt type")
97		}
98	
99		h := sha256.New()
100		_, _ = h.Write([]byte(docType))
101		_, _ = h.Write([]byte{0})
102		_, _ = h.Write(content)
103		return h.Sum(nil), nil
104	}
105	
106	// resolveTrimmedIdentity answers the submission-layer question for an id whose
107	// merge row is absent because compaction trimmed it. It returns true when the
108	// retained identity matches op's originating device and comparison content
109	// (an idempotent replay), an *ErrCRDTConflict when a retained identity exists
110	// but differs, and false with no error when no identity was retained (a
111	// genuinely new id, which proceeds through the normal acceptance path).
112	func resolveTrimmedIdentity(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, docType, mismatchReason string, op CRDTOp) (bool, error) {
113		digest, err := canonicalOpDigest(docType, op)
114		if err != nil {
115			return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{ID: op.ID, Reason: err.Error()}
116		}
117	
118		var existingDevice string
119		var existingDigest []byte
120		err = tx.QueryRow(
121			`SELECT device_id, digest FROM crdt_op_identities WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
122			documentID, op.ID,
123		).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingDigest)
124		switch {
125		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
126			return false, nil
127		case err != nil:
128			return false, err
129		}
130	
131		if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || !bytes.Equal(existingDigest, digest) {
132			return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{ID: op.ID, Reason: mismatchReason}
133		}
134		return true, nil
135	}
136	
137	// retainCRDTOpIdentity moves the comparable identity (device plus content
138	// digest) of one operation row compaction is about to drop into
139	// crdt_op_identities. A row is dropped at most once so the id is absent, but
140	// INSERT OR IGNORE keeps a repeat compaction finding the same row a harmless
141	// no-op.
142	func retainCRDTOpIdentity(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, docType string, op CRDTOp) error {
143		digest, err := canonicalOpDigest(docType, op)
144		if err != nil {
145			return err
146		}
147		_, err = tx.Exec(
148			`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO crdt_op_identities (document_id, id, device_id, digest) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
149			documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, digest,
150		)
151		return err
152	}

1	// Package service wires the HTTP surface and the durable store into one
2	// process: strict address binding, database open, a one-way readiness gate,
3	// actual-endpoint reporting and graceful shutdown.
4	//
5	// Startup order is deliberately load-bearing: the requested address is
6	// validated and bound first (so a fixed port that clashes fails before
7	// anything else happens, and :0 lets the kernel allocate one), and only after
8	// the database at the configured path has been created and opened does the
9	// instance become ready and print its endpoint. A failure at any step closes
10	// what was already acquired and returns an error, so no half-ready service is
11	// left behind. Two processes with different SYNC_ADDR/SYNC_DATA pairs share
12	// neither listener nor database.
13	package service
14	
15	import (
16		"context"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19		"log"
20		"net"
21		"net/http"
22		"os"
23		"path/filepath"
24		"strconv"
25		"sync/atomic"
26		"time"
27	
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/server"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
30	)
31	
32	const (
33		// defaultAddr is used only when SYNC_ADDR is unset.
34		defaultAddr = "127.0.0.1:8080"
35		// defaultDataPath is used only when SYNC_DATA is unset.
36		defaultDataPath = "data/sync.db"
37	
38		readHeaderTimeout = 10 * time.Second
39		shutdownTimeout   = 10 * time.Second
40	)
41	
42	// Options configures one isolated service instance.
43	type Options struct {
44		// Addr is the host:port to bind (SYNC_ADDR). Empty selects defaultAddr.
45		// A fixed address binds exactly that address with no fallback; port 0
46		// asks the kernel for a free port, reported through OnReady and the log.
47		Addr string
48		// DataPath is the SQLite database path (SYNC_DATA). Empty selects
49		// defaultDataPath; parent directories are created as needed.
50		DataPath string
51		// Logger receives the one startup line and shutdown diagnostics. nil
52		// uses the standard logger.
53		Logger *log.Logger
54		// OnReady, if set, is invoked with the actual dialable host:port after
55		// the listener is bound, the database is open and readiness is on.
56		OnReady func(actualAddr string)
57	}
58	
59	// Run starts one instance and blocks until ctx is canceled, then stops
60	// accepting new requests, drains in-flight ones and closes the database. A
61	// startup failure (bad address, port already in use, data directory or
62	// database that cannot be created or opened) returns before the instance is
63	// ready with every acquired resource already released.
64	func Run(ctx context.Context, opts Options) error {
65		addr := opts.Addr
66		if addr == "" {
67			addr = defaultAddr
68		}
69		dataPath := opts.DataPath
70		if dataPath == "" {
71			dataPath = defaultDataPath
72		}
73		logger := opts.Logger
74		if logger == nil {
75			logger = log.Default()
76		}
77	
78		// Validate first: a malformed SYNC_ADDR exits here, before any data
79		// directory is created or store opened, and never falls back.
80		host, _, err := parseAddr(addr)
81		if err != nil {
82			return err
83		}
84	
85		// Bind before opening the database. A fixed port that is already taken
86		// fails here with no files touched; :0 resolves to the allocated port.
87		ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", addr)
88		if err != nil {
89			return fmt.Errorf("listen on %s: %w", addr, err)
90		}
91		tcpAddr, ok := ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr)
92		if !ok {
93			_ = ln.Close()
94			return fmt.Errorf("listener on %s reported unexpected address %v", addr, ln.Addr())
95		}
96		// Report an address a client can actually dial. An empty host means the
97		// request was a wildcard bind (":port"); loopback always reaches it.
98		displayHost := host
99		if displayHost == "" {
100			displayHost = "127.0.0.1"
101		}
102		actualAddr := net.JoinHostPort(displayHost, strconv.Itoa(tcpAddr.Port))
103	
104		if dir := filepath.Dir(dataPath); dir != "." {
105			if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
106				_ = ln.Close()
107				return fmt.Errorf("create data directory %q: %w", dir, err)
108			}
109		}
110		st, err := store.Open(dataPath)
111		if err != nil {
112			_ = ln.Close()
113			return fmt.Errorf("open store at %q: %w", dataPath, err)
114		}
115	
116		// The gate covers the whole surface, /healthz included: nothing answers
117		// success until the database is open and the listener is serving.
118		var ready atomic.Bool
119		srv := &http.Server{
120			Handler:           server.NewHandlerWithReadiness(st, ready.Load),
121			ReadHeaderTimeout: readHeaderTimeout,
122		}
123		serveErr := make(chan error, 1)
124		go func() {
125			serveErr <- srv.Serve(ln)
126		}()
127	
128		ready.Store(true)
129		logger.Printf("sync service listening on %s (data: %s)", actualAddr, dataPath)
130		if opts.OnReady != nil {
131			opts.OnReady(actualAddr)
132		}
133	
134		// Block until shutdown is requested or the listener dies on its own.
135		var serveResult error
136		stoppedGracefully := false
137		select {
138		case <-ctx.Done():
139			stoppedGracefully = true
140		case serveResult = <-serveErr:
141		}
142	
143		// Shutdown closes the listener immediately (new connections are refused)
144		// and lets in-flight handlers finish before the store is closed. Waiting
145		// long polls are interrupted first so they answer instead of pinning the
146		// drain until their wait deadline. It is safe even when Serve has already
147		// returned on its own.
148		st.InterruptWaits()
149		shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), shutdownTimeout)
150		defer cancel()
151		if err := srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
152			logger.Printf("graceful shutdown did not complete: %v; forcing connections closed", err)
153			_ = srv.Close()
154		}
155		if stoppedGracefully {
156			serveResult = <-serveErr
157		}
158	
159		if serveResult != nil && !errors.Is(serveResult, http.ErrServerClosed) {
160			_ = st.Close()
161			return fmt.Errorf("serve on %s: %w", actualAddr, serveResult)
162		}
163		if err := st.Close(); err != nil {
164			// Shutdown was requested and all handlers have drained; report the
165			// close problem without pretending requests were lost.
166			logger.Printf("close store at %q: %v", dataPath, err)
167		}
168		return nil
169	}
170	
171	// parseAddr validates that addr is a host:port with a TCP port in range. Port
172	// 0 is legal and means "let the kernel choose". Anything else is a startup
173	// error rather than a cue to fall back to a default.
174	func parseAddr(addr string) (host string, port int, err error) {
175		host, portStr, splitErr := net.SplitHostPort(addr)
176		if splitErr != nil {
177			return "", 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid SYNC_ADDR %q: expected host:port: %v", addr, splitErr)
178		}
179		port, convErr := strconv.Atoi(portStr)
180		if convErr != nil || port < 0 || port > 65535 {
181			return "", 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid SYNC_ADDR %q: port must be an integer between 0 and 65535", addr)
182		}
183		return host, port, nil
184	}

255	// the pre-existing surface is unchanged. The new device/session families are
256	// stricter: any doubled slash (an empty deviceId, sessionId or documentId
257	// segment) or a trailing slash (an empty final id) is a 400 JSON error.
258	func emptyIDGuard(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
259		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
260			p := r.URL.Path
261	
262			documentSegmentEmpty := strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/documents//")
263			newFamilySegmentEmpty := false
264			if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/devices/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/") {
265				newFamilySegmentEmpty = strings.Contains(p, "//") || strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
266			}
267	
268			if documentSegmentEmpty || newFamilySegmentEmpty || malformedNewDocumentPath(p) || malformedSubscribePath(p) || malformedSessionCRDTPath(p) || malformedCRDTPath(p) {
269				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "path identifiers must be non-empty strings")
270				return
271			}
272			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
273		})
274	}

276	// malformedNewDocumentPath reports whether p targets one of the new
277	// long-poll/replay endpoints but is not that endpoint's exact location: a
278	// missing/empty segment, a trailing slash, extra segments, or a "poll"/"replay"
279	// segment in a position short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer
280	// those with a 301 redirect or a plain-text 404/405; the new endpoints promise
281	// a JSON error and never a redirect, so every such path is a malformed 400.
282	//
283	// Keywords are matched only past the documentID position, so documents that
284	// happen to be named "poll" or "replay" keep their ordinary merge/snapshot/
285	// changes routes.
286	func malformedNewDocumentPath(p string) bool {
287		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
288		if !ok {
289			return false
290		}
291		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
292	
293		// Poll endpoint: "poll" must be exactly the third segment, after a
294		// non-empty documentID and "changes".
295		for i, seg := range segs {
296			if seg == "poll" && i > 0 {
297				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
298			}
299		}
300		// Replay endpoint: "replay" must be exactly the second segment, after a
301		// non-empty documentID.
302		for i, seg := range segs {
303			if seg == "replay" && i > 0 {
304				return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
305			}
306		}
307		return false
308	}
309	
310	// malformedSubscribePath reports whether p targets the WebSocket subscription
311	// endpoint but is not at its exact location
312	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/subscribe): a
313	// missing "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "subscribe"
314	// segment short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
315	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of this endpoint must be a JSON 400
316	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
317	//
318	// "subscribe" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the endpoint's
319	// terminal segment position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or
320	// document identifier literally named "subscribe" occupies an identifier
321	// position (index 0 or 2) and is therefore left to the ordinary
322	// changes/subscribe routes like any other id.
323	func malformedSubscribePath(p string) bool {
324		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
325		if !ok {
326			return false
327		}
328		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
329		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
330		// has its own guard; "subscribe" there is not the changes-subscribe
331		// keyword.
332		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
333			return false
334		}
335		for i, seg := range segs {
336			if seg != "subscribe" {
337				continue
338			}
339			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
340			// "subscribe" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
341			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
342				continue
343			}
344			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
345			// "subscribe" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
346			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
347			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
348				segs[0] != "" &&
349				segs[1] == "documents" &&
350				segs[2] != "" &&
351				segs[3] == "changes" {
352				return false
353			}
354			return true
355		}
356		return false
357	}
358	
359	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
360	// namespace but is not at one of its two exact locations:
361	//
362	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
363	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
364	//
365	// a missing "state"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or a "crdt" segment
366	// in the keyword position (immediately past the document identifier) short of
367	// one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer those with a
368	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a JSON 400
369	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
370	//
371	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
372	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
373	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
374	// keeps its ordinary routes.
375	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
376		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
377		if !ok {
378			return false
379		}
380		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
381		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
382			return false
383		}
384		// Keyword position reached. The state read is exactly
385		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state; the subscription adds
386		// one trailing "subscribe" segment.
387		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
388			segs[0] != "" &&
389			segs[2] != "" &&
390			segs[4] == "state"
391		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
392			segs[0] != "" &&
393			segs[2] != "" &&
394			segs[4] == "state" &&
395			segs[5] == "subscribe"
396		return !(validState || validSubscribe)
397	}

409	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
410	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
411	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
412	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
413	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
414	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
415	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
416		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
417		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
418			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
419			return false
420		}
421	
422		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
423		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
424		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
425			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
426			return false
427		}
428		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
429		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
430			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
431			return false
432		}
433		return true
434	}

500	func handlePostChanges(s *store.Store, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
501		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern guarantees non-empty
502	
503		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
504		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
505			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
506			return
507		}
508	
509		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
510		var req postRequest
511		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
512		if err := dec.Decode(&req); err != nil {
513			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
514			return
515		}
516		// Reject trailing data after the JSON object.
517		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
518			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
519			return
520		}
521	
522		if req.DeviceID == "" {
523			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
524			return
525		}
526		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
527			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
528			return
529		}
530	
531		changes := make([]store.Change, len(req.Changes))
532		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
533		for i, c := range req.Changes {
534			if c.ID == "" {
535				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
536				return
537			}
538			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
539				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
540				return
541			}
542			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
543				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
544				return
545			}
546			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
547			changes[i] = store.Change{ID: c.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: c.Payload}
548		}
549	
550		results, err := s.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
551		if err != nil {
552			var conflict *store.ErrConflict
553			if errors.As(err, &conflict) {
554				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "change id already exists with different deviceId or payload: "+conflict.ID)
555				return
556			}
557			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to commit changes")
558			return
559		}
560	
561		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
562	}

571		}

573		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
574		var req mergeRequest

576		if err := dec.Decode(&req); err != nil {

610			return
611		}

613		result, err := s.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, store.Change{

630			}

768	// handleSetPermission grants or revokes a registered device's access to one
769	// document. Devices start authorized, so the first revoke is the first write;
770	// repeating the current state is idempotent (changed=false). A rejected
771	// request (bad content type, malformed JSON, trailing content, empty or
772	// mistyped fields, unknown action) is a 400 JSON error and writes nothing; an
773	// unregistered device is a 404 JSON error.
774	func handleSetPermission(s *store.Store, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
775		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern guarantees non-empty
776	
777		var req permissionRequest
778		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
779			return
780		}
781		if req.DeviceID == "" {
782			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
783			return
784		}
785		var authorized bool
786		switch req.Action {
787		case "grant":
788			authorized = true
789		case "revoke":
790			authorized = false
791		default:
792			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, `action must be "grant" or "revoke"`)
793			return
794		}
795	
796		changed, err := s.SetDocumentPermission(documentID, req.DeviceID, authorized)
797		if err != nil {
798			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound) {
799				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
800				return
801			}
802			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to update permission")
803			return
804		}
805	
806		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
807			"deviceId":   req.DeviceID,
808			"authorized": authorized,
809			"changed":    changed,
810		})
811	}

813	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
814	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.
815	func parseCursorPath(raw string) (int64, bool) {
816		if raw == "" {
817			return 0, false
818		}
819		for _, c := range raw {
820			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
821				return 0, false
822			}
823		}
824		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
825		if err != nil {
826			return 0, false
827		}
828		return n, true
829	}
830	
831	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
832	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
833		var n int64
834		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
835			return 0, false
836		}
837		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
838		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
